persuasionAngle.rationale: This persona's core fear is that Patagonia's model only works because Chouinard is exceptional, making it irrelevant to their reality. By exposing the actual trade-offs and costs Patagonia accepted early on, we prove the model is replicable but requires specific sacrifices—giving them a concrete framework instead of inspiration porn.
persuasionAngle.psychFramework: Existential proof through disclosed sacrifice—showing what Patagonia gave up early validates that values-driven scale is possible for mortals willing to pay similar costs

creative.headline: We turned down $100M in revenue
creative.provocativeHook: Here's what saying no to fast fashion actually costs
creative.postText:
1996: Patagonia could have licensed our name to mass retailers. The revenue projections were staggering. We said no. Twenty-six years later, that decision saved the brand but cost us billions.

Most 'purpose-driven' companies never face this choice. We did. #BCorps #PurposeDriven
creative.cta: What revenue have you walked away from to stay true to your values
creative.tone: Unflinchingly honest about real costs, no martyrdom or virtue signaling, just founder-to-founder acknowledgment that values have a price tag and Patagonia paid it
